surveyProject.title: In-Vehicle Cyberthreat Detection for Vehicle Fleets

question.lead:
Survey on Vehicle Log-Sources for Cyberthreat Detection



This survey is conducted as part of a bachelor's thesis on Real-Time In-Vehicle Cyberthreat Detection for Vehicle Fleets and takes
~30 minutes to complete.

The purpose of this survey is to validate and refine the overview of log-sources with input from domain experts. Within the scope of this study, domain experts are defined as individuals with a minimum of one year of experience in automotive IT security.


Specifically, the survey aims to:
  • Assess whether the identified log sources and categorization are correct
  • Identify missing log sources

Your feedback will help improve cyberthreat detection in vehicles by assessing potential vehicle log sources that can aid in detecting attackers.

All data is transmitted anonymously, cannot be traced back to the participants, and will be used for academic purposes only.

Please read the following statements carefully and indicate whether you agree.

Participation in this study is only possible if you agree to all statements.

question.lead:
Vehicle Log-Source Validation

The log-source structure is based on the following attack surface layers:
  • Vehicle Layer
  • Proximity Layer
  • Backend and Cloud Layer
  • Network Layer

The full Vehicle Log Sources Overview can be found here.

Within the taxonomy, components are assigned to the layer/component in which they are most predominant, even if they could be associated with multiple layers/components.



The green rectangles denote Traditional Enterprise-IT, while the blue rectangles represent In-Vehicle (automotive-native) Systems.
